subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a core admin-scoped shell-to-Control-UI notification surface, and if so what auth scope, payload, targeting, and rate-limit rules should it own?
rationale: The requested behavior is not just a missing command; it creates a new trusted broadcast path into connected UI clients and overlaps existing notification architecture work.

options.title: Design the core contract first
options.body: Define the Gateway RPC/event, admin scope, sanitization, rate limiting, delivery semantics, and UI rendering before any implementation PR.

options.title: Fold into broader UI notifications
options.body: Make the Control UI notification/toast tracker canonical and keep this issue as the shell/admin trigger requirement for that architecture.

options.title: Reject core notify for now
options.body: Keep shell alerts on existing external/plugin paths unless maintainers decide the security and UX cost is worth a built-in surface.

recommendation.title: Design the core contract first
recommendation.body: Define the Gateway RPC/event, admin scope, sanitization, rate limiting, delivery semantics, and UI rendering before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans Gateway authorization, CLI API, and Control UI product boundaries where recent history points to steipete as the best routing candidate.
